newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank to study money policy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank to study money policy.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Saturday it would study whether recent surges in share prices were directly related to its loose monetary policy, but added that it had no immediate intention to tighten liquidity.
"We have no immediate plan to change our monetary policy, but we do not want to see liquidity become too loose," deputy bank governor Hsu Chia-tung told reporters.
The central bank said early on Saturday it would issue T$5.0 billion in 10-day negotiable certificates of deposits (NCDs) during the morning to mop up excess liquidity.
Taiwan share prices surged to yet another 22-month high at 6,842.16 at Saturday's close on hectic turnover of T$103 billion.
Securities analysts have said the market's recent bull run was fuelled partly by abundant liquidity as the result of the central bank's loose monetary policy.
Hsu said the central bank was not convinced of this.
"We have asked the relevant departments to study whether there is a connection between the red-hot stock market and monetary policy," Hsu said.
"The stock market should not be over-heated."
